page: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.large is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs via an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor clocked at 5.0 GHz. Supporting vector instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, the processor couples high frequency with modern execution capabilities. A standout feature of this hardware configuration is its memory density, offering 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, equating to an unusually large 32.0 GB allocation per core. The server includes 158 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results highlight extraordinary single-threaded compute and compression speeds. The instance lands in the top tier for single-core execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 3098.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 4209.88, alongside top-tier gzip compression throughput of 45.88 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded output aligns with the middle range due to the compact 2-vCPU hardware footprint, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 5555.0 and stress-ng multi-core reaching 8390.88. Evaluated uncached large-block memory bandwidth sustains 81.36 GB/sec for reads and 65.84 GB/sec for writes. Workloads requiring dense parallel execution, such as ray tracing and prompt processing on 7B LLMs, show modest results.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the x8aedz.large offers strong value for software requiring vast memory headroom without requiring high core counts. The combination of 64 GB RAM, high single-thread clock rates, and integrated NVMe storage makes this server profile well aligned for in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, lightweight relational or key-value databases, and single-stream data ingestion tasks that do not justify larger multi-core instances.
